titulo: PAU 2027 · Cantabria · Lengua Extranjera II: Inglés
instrucciones: El examen consta de dos apartados. En la Parte 1, elige una sola opción de comprensión lectora (Option 1 u Option 2) y responde únicamente a las preguntas de esa opción. En la Parte 2, elige una de las dos propuestas de expresión escrita y redacta un único texto de 120-150 palabras. Los textos de hasta 200 palabras no serán penalizados. No firmes la composición. La puntuación total es de 10 puntos: 7 puntos en la Parte 1 y 3 puntos en la Parte 2. En las preguntas que exigen elegir un número determinado de respuestas, si respondes a más de las indicadas, solo se corregirán las primeras, siguiendo el orden en que aparecen.

preguntas.enunciado:
PART 1 [7 points]. Written comprehension. Choose Option 1 or Option 2 and answer only the questions for your chosen option.

OPTION 1. A cooler walk to school

1. After a week of unusually hot weather, a group of parents in the Spanish town of Bellavista asked the local secondary school whether the route with more shade was actually cooler for students walking to class. The school’s science teacher suggested that students investigate the question instead of relying on impressions. The project was designed to give families and town planners useful information about the school journey.

2. Eighteen students and four local residents volunteered. They marked 20 measuring points along two routes: a direct road and a longer path beside a canal. On ten dry school afternoons, at 3:15 p.m., the teams used the same infrared thermometer to record the pavement temperature at each point. They also noted where trees or buildings provided shade. The results were added to a map that anyone can view on the school website.

3. The canal path took six minutes longer to walk, but its average pavement temperature was eight degrees Celsius lower than that of the direct route. The hottest reading came from an unshaded bus stop on the direct road. The teacher warned that the short study could not show what temperatures would be like throughout the year, but the comparison gave the council a practical starting point.

4. The council has included 14 new trees and two drinking fountains in its next budget, with the work planned for the autumn. Families can scan a QR code at the school entrance to open the project map. The students hope the information will help people choose a more comfortable route and encourage the town to consider shade when it improves public spaces.

Question 1 [2 points]. Indicate clearly by writing TRUE or FALSE whether each statement is true or false according to the text. For every answer, copy the sentence or part of the text that justifies it. The evidence must be relevant and grammatically and lexically coherent. Each item is worth 0.5 points.
A. The project began after parents asked whether shade made a difference to the journey to school.
B. The students took pavement-temperature readings both in the morning and in the afternoon.
C. The canal path was shorter and had a higher average pavement temperature than the direct route.
D. The council has included both trees and drinking fountains in its next budget.
preguntas.solucion:
### Respuestas y justificación

**A. TRUE.** “After a week of unusually hot weather, a group of parents in the Spanish town of Bellavista asked the local secondary school whether the route with more shade was actually cooler for students walking to class.”

**B. FALSE.** “On ten dry school afternoons, at 3:15 p.m., the teams used the same infrared thermometer to record the pavement temperature at each point.”

**C. FALSE.** “The canal path took six minutes longer to walk, but its average pavement temperature was eight degrees Celsius lower than that of the direct route.”

**D. TRUE.** “The council has included 14 new trees and two drinking fountains in its next budget, with the work planned for the autumn.”

### Corrección
Cada apartado vale 0,5 puntos. Se concede la puntuación del apartado cuando se indica correctamente TRUE o FALSE y se aporta una cita pertinente del texto que lo justifique, con formulación gramatical y léxicamente coherente. Puntuación máxima: 2 puntos.
preguntas.resultado: A TRUE; B FALSE; C FALSE; D TRUE.
preguntas.criterios: 0,5 puntos por apartado: identificación correcta como TRUE/FALSE y evidencia textual relevante, gramatical y léxicamente coherente. Total: 2 puntos.

preguntas.enunciado:
Question 2 [2 points]. Choose and answer only TWO of the following questions in your own words according to the text in Option 1. Each answer is worth 1 point.
A. Why did the school decide to investigate the two routes?
B. How did the volunteers collect the temperature information? Give at least two details.
C. What improvements has the council included in its next budget, and when are they planned?
preguntas.solucion: No se puede resolver con rigor porque no se ha incluido el texto de la Option 1. Las tres preguntas exigen información específica de ese texto; responder sin él supondría inventar datos. Para completar el ejercicio, hay que elegir solo dos preguntas y contestarlas con palabras propias, basándose en el pasaje.
preguntas.resultado: Falta el texto de la Option 1 para determinar las respuestas.
preguntas.criterios: 2 puntos en total: 1 punto por cada una de las dos respuestas elegidas. Sin el texto de referencia no es posible asignar una puntuación fiable.

preguntas.enunciado:
Question 3 [1.5 points]. Find in the text in Option 1 a word or phrase that corresponds to each meaning. Each item is worth 0.375 points.
A. A period of unusually hot weather [paragraph 1]
B. People who offer to do something without being paid [paragraph 2]
C. To examine two or more things to see how they are similar or different [paragraph 2]
D. Money available for planned spending [paragraph 4]
preguntas.solucion: Método: relaciono cada definición con su equivalente léxico y compruebo que encaje con la función gramatical indicada. A. «A period of unusually hot weather» corresponde a **heatwave**. B. «People who offer to do something without being paid» corresponde a **volunteers**. C. «To examine two or more things to see how they are similar or different» corresponde a **compare**. D. «Money available for planned spending» corresponde a **budget**. Comprobación: las cuatro opciones coinciden con las definiciones; al no estar incluido el texto de Option 1, no puedo verificar que sean exactamente las palabras o expresiones que aparecen en él.
preguntas.resultado: A. heatwave; B. volunteers; C. compare; D. budget.
preguntas.criterios: 0,375 puntos por cada correspondencia correcta, hasta un máximo de 1,5 puntos. La respuesta debe coincidir con la palabra o expresión que aparece en el texto de Option 1; sin ese texto, las propuestas son candidatos semánticos y no se puede confirmar su exactitud.

preguntas.enunciado:
Question 4 [1.5 points]. Choose the correct answer according to the text in Option 1.
What did the students find when they compared the two routes?
A. The canal path took six minutes less to walk and had cooler pavement.
B. The direct route was cooler because it had more trees beside the road.
C. The canal path took six minutes longer, and its average pavement temperature was lower.
D. Both routes had the same average pavement temperature, although one was longer.
preguntas.solucion:
### Resolución
Comparamos las dos características que pregunta el enunciado: el tiempo de recorrido y la temperatura media del pavimento.

- La opción **C** afirma que el camino junto al canal tardó **seis minutos más** y que su pavimento tuvo una temperatura media menor.
- La opción **A** invierte la duración y atribuye al camino del canal un tiempo menor.
- La opción **B** atribuye el menor calor a la ruta directa y añade una explicación sobre los árboles.
- La opción **D** sostiene que las temperaturas medias fueron iguales.

Por tanto, la respuesta que recoge la comparación indicada es **C**. Como comprobación, sus dos datos —más tiempo en el camino del canal y menor temperatura media— aparecen juntos en esa opción, sin invertir la duración ni afirmar que las temperaturas fueran iguales.
preguntas.resultado: C. El camino junto al canal tardó seis minutos más y tuvo una temperatura media del pavimento menor.
preguntas.criterios: 1,5 puntos por seleccionar C. 0 puntos por elegir otra opción o dejarla en blanco; no se asigna puntuación parcial en esta pregunta de elección múltiple.

preguntas.enunciado:
PART 1 [7 points]. Written comprehension. Choose Option 1 or Option 2 and answer only the questions for your chosen option.

OPTION 2. A quieter museum visit

1. Families visiting the Harbour Museum in the town of Llevant told staff that busy galleries could sometimes make a visit difficult. In response, the museum tested a monthly session called Quiet Start. The aim was to make the collection more comfortable to explore, while keeping the museum open to anyone who wanted to attend.

2. Quiet Start takes place on the first Sunday of each month, from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m. Recorded announcements are switched off, and the lights in the galleries are dimmed; safety lights in corridors remain fully on. The museum limits attendance to 60 people. Visitors can take a break in a quiet room and return to the galleries whenever they are ready. Booking online is recommended, although visitors can also come without a reservation if there is space.

3. Before the trial began, a local accessibility group trained 12 museum employees. Staff learnt how to explain the layout clearly and offer visitors ear defenders. No one has to provide proof of a disability to attend, and the ticket price is the same as for a regular visit.

4. After six months, 52 households completed a feedback form, and 45 said their family had been able to stay longer than during a usual visit. The museum has therefore decided to continue Quiet Start once a month. It also plans to produce a tactile map of the building next year, based on suggestions from visitors.

Question 1 [2 points]. Indicate clearly by writing TRUE or FALSE whether each statement is true or false according to the text. For every answer, copy the sentence or part of the text that justifies it. The evidence must be relevant and grammatically and lexically coherent. Each item is worth 0.5 points.
A. The museum introduced Quiet Start after families gave staff feedback about their visits.
B. All the lights in the museum are switched off during Quiet Start.
C. Visitors have to show proof of a disability before they can attend a session.
D. A local accessibility group trained some of the museum’s employees.
preguntas.solucion:
### A. TRUE
**Justificación:** “Families visiting the Harbour Museum in the town of Llevant told staff that busy galleries could sometimes make a visit difficult. In response, the museum tested a monthly session called Quiet Start.”

### B. FALSE
**Justificación:** “The lights in the galleries are dimmed; safety lights in corridors remain fully on.” Por tanto, no se apagan todas las luces.

### C. FALSE
**Justificación:** “No one has to provide proof of a disability to attend.”

### D. TRUE
**Justificación:** “Before the trial began, a local accessibility group trained 12 museum employees.”
preguntas.resultado: A: TRUE; B: FALSE; C: FALSE; D: TRUE. Puntuación: 2/2.
preguntas.criterios: 0,5 puntos por cada apartado, siempre que se indique correctamente TRUE o FALSE y se aporte una cita del texto pertinente, gramatical y léxicamente coherente. Total: 2 puntos.

preguntas.enunciado:
Question 2 [2 points]. Choose and answer only TWO of the following questions in your own words according to the text in Option 2. Each answer is worth 1 point.
A. Give two changes the museum makes during Quiet Start.
B. What can visitors do if they need a break during their visit?
C. What did the feedback forms reveal, and what did the museum decide to do as a result?
preguntas.solucion: No se incluye el texto de la Option 2. Por tanto, no es posible determinar con rigor qué dos cambios realiza el museo durante Quiet Start, qué pueden hacer los visitantes para descansar ni qué revelaron los formularios. Para responder sin inventar información, hace falta el texto de referencia.
preguntas.resultado: No se puede determinar la respuesta sin el texto de la Option 2.
preguntas.criterios: La pregunta vale 2 puntos: 1 punto por cada una de las dos respuestas elegidas, siempre que sea correcta y esté expresada con palabras propias. Sin el texto de referencia no se pueden establecer respuestas ni asignar esos puntos.

preguntas.enunciado:
Question 3 [1.5 points]. Find in the text in Option 2 a word or phrase that corresponds to each meaning. Each item is worth 0.375 points.
A. Made less bright [paragraph 2]
B. A maximum number allowed [paragraph 2]
C. Evidence that confirms something [paragraph 3]
D. To continue doing something [paragraph 4]
preguntas.solucion: No se puede determinar la respuesta exacta porque no se ha incluido el texto de la Option 2. Las equivalencias semánticas que habría que localizar son: A) «hecho menos brillante»; B) «número máximo permitido»; C) «prueba que confirma algo»; D) «continuar haciendo algo». Sin el texto no es posible verificar qué palabras o expresiones aparecen en los párrafos indicados.
preguntas.resultado: Falta el texto de la Option 2 para identificar las cuatro respuestas exactas.
preguntas.criterios: Cada respuesta correcta vale 0,375 puntos; total: 1,5 puntos. Sin el texto de referencia no se pueden identificar ni puntuar las respuestas exactas.

preguntas.enunciado:
Question 4 [1.5 points]. Choose the correct answer according to the text in Option 2.
What did 45 of the 52 households report?
A. Their family had stayed longer than on a usual visit.
B. They had booked a place for every monthly session.
C. Their family had visited the museum for the first time.
D. They wanted the museum to switch off all its lights.
preguntas.solucion:
### Resolución por eliminación

1. La pregunta pide identificar qué comunicaron 45 de los 52 hogares.
2. La opción que recoge ese dato es **A**: la familia se quedó más tiempo que en una visita habitual.
3. Las opciones B, C y D atribuyen a los hogares reservas para todas las sesiones, una primera visita o el deseo de apagar todas las luces; no corresponden al dato preguntado.
4. **Comprobación:** la opción A responde directamente a qué reportaron esos 45 hogares.

**Respuesta: A.**
preguntas.resultado: A. Su familia se había quedado más tiempo que en una visita habitual.
preguntas.criterios: 1,5 puntos por seleccionar la opción A. 0 puntos por elegir otra opción o no responder.

preguntas.enunciado:
PART 2 [3 points]. Written production. Choose ONE of the two options below and write a short composition of 120-150 words. Compositions of up to 200 words will not be penalized. Do not sign your composition.

Option 1. Email
You are taking part in a student exchange. Your exchange partner, Sam, has written to you: Our class is making a short podcast about free activities for teenagers. What could we do in your town after school? Tell me about one place or activity, explain how to get there, and say why young people would enjoy it. Write your reply.

Option 2. For-and-against essay
Should towns make the streets immediately around schools pedestrian-only at school drop-off and pick-up times? Write a for-and-against essay giving reasons and examples to support your ideas.
preguntas.solucion:
### Desarrollo
1. **Opción elegida:** 1, email a Sam.
2. **Contenido requerido:** se propone una actividad gratuita, se indica cómo llegar y se explica por qué puede gustar a los jóvenes.
3. **Composición (135 palabras):**

Hi Sam,

There’s a great free place for teenagers in my town: Riverside Park. After school, we can play basketball on the outdoor court, ride our bikes along the river, or just meet friends and listen to music. The park is open to everyone, and you don’t need to book anything.

To get there from our school, walk down King Street until you reach the library. Turn left at the traffic lights and follow the riverside path for about ten minutes. The park entrance is opposite the sports centre, so it’s easy to find.

I think young people would enjoy it because there’s something for everyone, whether you like being active or prefer relaxing outdoors. It’s also a good way to spend time together without spending money. We could even record some podcast interviews there!

4. **Corrección:** cumple la extensión, responde a todos los apartados y mantiene un registro adecuado para un email informal. **Nota estimada: 3/3.**

### Criterios de corrección aplicados
Desglose orientativo, ya que la rúbrica concreta puede variar según la comunidad autónoma: adecuación y contenido, 1 punto; organización y cohesión, 0,5 puntos; vocabulario y adecuación léxica, 0,5 puntos; gramática, ortografía y puntuación, 1 punto.
preguntas.resultado: Opción 1: email de 135 palabras; nota estimada: 3/3.
preguntas.criterios: Adecuación y contenido: 1 punto; organización y cohesión: 0,5 puntos; vocabulario y adecuación léxica: 0,5 puntos; gramática, ortografía y puntuación: 1 punto. Total: 3 puntos. La respuesta modelo obtiene 3/3.
